1.0.0.en: Beginning with the conjunction "and" shows that the Book of Judges is a continuation of the Book of Joshua. Joshua had divided the Promised Land among the tribes, but the whole land had not yet been cleared of its pagan inhabitants, and this was left for the tribes to carry out. So after the death of Joshua, the children of Israel asked which of the tribes should begin the fight against the Canaanites, the original inhabitants of the land, who were still living in some regions and had recovered some parts of what the children of Israel had possessed. The inquiry of God was made through the high priest in the tabernacle of meeting.

1.1.0.en: God answered by choosing the tribe of Judah to begin fighting the Canaanites. The reason for choosing this tribe is that it was the most numerous of the tribes, and also that from it would come Christ, who overcomes Satan and binds him by the Cross.

1.2.0.en: The tribe of Judah asked the tribe of Simeon to go out with it to fight the Canaanites, on the condition that Judah would go out and take part with Simeon in its coming wars against the Canaanites, for the following reasons:

1.2.1.en: 1- The tribe of Simeon lived next to the tribe of Judah.

1.2.2.en: 2- Simeon and Judah were both sons of Leah.

1.2.3.en: 3- Simeon was a small tribe, so that it would not feel its weakness, Judah included it in the war with him, and afterward the great tribe of Judah would share with its brother in its wars to help it win the war. This is a kind of encouragement for the smaller and the weaker. The tribe of Simeon agreed to take part with the tribe of Judah in the war.

1.2.4.en: How beautiful it is that you encourage the small of soul and include them in the work with you, even in a small way, to commend and honor them, just as God includes you in His service and blesses you and glorifies you.

1.3.0.en: The Perizzites: one of the original inhabitants of the land. They were the dwellers of villages, for the meaning of their name is villagers.

1.3.1.en: Bezek: a city in the tribe of Judah, about 24 km northwest of Jerusalem.

1.3.2.en: The tribes of Judah and Simeon advanced to the city of Bezek and fought the Canaanites and the Perizzites who lived there. They defeated them and killed ten thousand of them.

1.4.0.en: Adoni: a word meaning lord. So Adoni-bezek means the king or lord of the city of Bezek.

1.4.1.en: Thumbs: the plural of thumb, the big digit of the hand or the foot, which is regarded as essential for gripping weapons in war or for walking.

1.4.2.en: During the war of Judah and Simeon against Bezek, they seized its king, called Adoni-bezek, who was famous for humiliating the kings he defeated: he would cut off the thumbs of their hands so that they could not grip weapons, and the thumbs of their feet so that they could not run. So they did to him as he had done to the kings he had defeated before, and cut off the thumbs of his hands and feet, perhaps so that this might lead him to humility, repentance and faith.

1.5.0.en: Adoni-bezek remembered what he had done to the kings he had defeated during his life, who were seventy kings. This shows the extent of his strength in war, yet he was defeated before the power of God. It was a humiliation of those kings that he made them sit under his table like dogs while he ate, to throw them some food, and because of his injustice to them, God decided to take vengeance on him in the same way. The Jews brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.

1.6.s.en: (2) The capture of Jerusalem, Hebron and Debir

1.6.0.en: Joshua had captured Jerusalem, but it seems that some of its original, pagan inhabitants were able to retake it, so the tribe of Judah fought against it, captured it, and burned it with fire, together with the pagans in it, as a lesson to others so that the pagans would fear. It should be noted that the burning of the city was only partial, as is shown by the fact that they lived in it afterward and that some Jebusites also lived with them (v. 21). The tribe of Judah captured Jerusalem, but did not take the stronghold of Zion adjoining the city, in which the Jebusites remained; but King David was later able to capture the city and the stronghold and drive out the Jebusites completely (2 Sam 5:6, 7).

1.7.0.en: The mountain: the mountainous lands lying south of Jerusalem, including Bethlehem and Hebron. The south: the dry lands lying between the Dead Sea on the east and the Mediterranean on the west, and from Hebron on the north to the wilderness on the south, called the Negev desert (Josh 15:21) (Map 10). The valley: the valleys that are in the tribe of Judah.

1.7.1.en: After that Judah fought the Canaanites in various places in the mountains, the southern deserts and the valleys, and took possession of their lands.

1.8.0.en: Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai: chiefs of the tribes of the Anakim, who were among the original inhabitants of the land and were distinguished by strength.

1.8.1.en: Kirjath-sepher: that is, the city of the book, a city distinguished by learning and knowledge.

1.8.2.en: This portion was mentioned earlier in the Book of Joshua (ch. 14:13, 14; 15:16-19), and it is mentioned here to complete the account of the victories of the tribe of Judah and its leader Caleb, in order to show the power of God supporting them. So refer to the explanation of this portion in the Book of Joshua.

1.8.3.en: If you are obedient to God and rely on Him, be sure that He supports you in every circumstance of life, however much the wicked oppose you or seize your rights. God keeps them away from you because of their wickedness and upholds you as long as you hold fast to your purity and righteousness.

1.9.s.en: (3) The rest of the wars of Judah

1.9.0.en: The Kenites: they are the descendants of Moses' father-in-law. The meaning of Kenite is smith, since some of them worked in smithing. Many tribes branched out from them, most of which were at peace with the Jews, such as the Rechabites, and lived beside them (Jer 35), but a few of them were wicked, and these are the ones God promised Abraham that He would drive out (Gen 15). The Kenites were dwelling in the city of palm trees when the tribe of Judah was carrying out its wars, and when the city was struck they fled from it and settled in the desert lands lying west of the Dead Sea and east of Jerusalem, where pasture is abundant, and they lived there with the peoples of those regions, who were Canaanites.

1.10.0.en: Judah and Simeon continued their wars and defeated the Canaanites who lived in Zephath and killed its people.

1.11.0.en: Then the tribe of Judah, with the tribe of Simeon, faced the Philistines in three of their five great cities, which are Gaza, Ashkelon and Ekron, together with the small towns surrounding each of them, and they captured them all.

1.12.0.en: The Lord was their helper, so they succeeded in possessing the mountain lands, but they were unable to possess the plain of the valley because the Canaanites there were armed with chariots of iron. The faith of Judah and Simeon weakened and they were afraid before these chariots, especially since the Philistines had monopolized the making of iron until the days of David the prophet (1 Sam 13:19-22), who defeated them and introduced the use and manufacture of iron in Israel.

1.13.0.en: The inspired writer returns here once more to mention the giving of the city of Hebron to Caleb, which happened in the days of Joshua, repeating the account of the driving out of the three sons of Anak, in honor of Caleb, who was among the spies whom Moses sent to spy out the land and who declared that God was able to give them the land despite the strength of its inhabitants (Josh 14:13, 14; 15:13-14).

1.13.1.en: As long as God is with you, do not be troubled by the strength of those who oppose you or by their threats, but trust in His power and seek Him earnestly, and you will walk in assurance all your days.

1.14.0.en: Unto this day: that is, until the time the book was written, and this confirms that the book was written by Samuel the prophet before David became king.

1.14.1.en: Jerusalem lay on the border of Judah, so it was shared between the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, the southern part belonging to Judah and the northern to Benjamin. Both Judah and Benjamin were slack in driving out the Jebusites who were in Jerusalem, and this was a failure on their part to keep the commandment of the Lord. They thought that by leaving these peoples they would obtain tribute from them and make them work for them. David later drove them out (2 Sam 5).

1.15.s.en: (4) Accounts of the wars of the tribe of Joseph

1.15.0.en: The two brothers, that is, the tribe of Ephraim and the half-tribe of Manasseh (the one living west of the Jordan), joined together in fighting Bethel, and the Lord was with them, so they captured it.

1.16.0.en: The two tribes assigned a group of spies to learn the information needed about the city, to make it easier to fight it and capture it, which is what was done, and still is done, in many wars. The name of the city was formerly Luz.

1.17.0.en: While watching the city, the spies saw a man coming out of it, and they asked him to show them the entrance to the city so that they could enter it, and they promised him a reward for guiding them.

1.18.0.en: The man responded to their request and showed them the way into the city, which enabled the sons of Joseph to capture it and kill its inhabitants. They rewarded the man who showed them the entrance by leaving him alive, he and his family, and not harming him, as they did to the rest of the people of the city.

1.19.0.en: As soon as he was given his freedom, the man went to the land of the Hittites, who lived in some regions of the land of Palestine (as they also lived in scattered places in Syria and Turkey). There he built a city and called it Luz, after the city of Luz which he had left, whose name was changed to Bethel. It should be noted that the pagan man who guided the Jews into the city went off afterward to live with the pagans and did not believe in God, who helped the Jews to possess the city. He saw God's victory and did not believe, as many do today: they guide others to the upright life, but they themselves do not repent.

1.19.1.en: As the tribes of Ephraim and the half-tribe of Manasseh cooperated in their war against Bethel, may you also cooperate with your spiritual brothers, encouraging them and supporting them in their battles with the devil, for God rejoices in this love of yours and rewards you with many blessings.

1.20.s.en: (5) The failure of the tribes to drive out the pagan peoples

1.20.0.en: Beth-shean: a city about 6.5 km west of the Jordan River.

1.20.1.en: Taanach: a city in the middle of Palestine, about 21 km from Nazareth.

1.20.2.en: Dor: a city lying about 9 km southeast of Nazareth.

1.20.3.en: Ibleam: a city lying south of Jenin.

1.20.4.en: Megiddo: a city southeast of Haifa (Maps 10, 12). Just as the children of Israel of the other tribes failed to drive out the pagan inhabitants, so also the sons of the tribe of Manasseh did the same: they did not drive out the pagan peoples from the cities and villages they had taken, which were Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam and Megiddo. So the Canaanites resolved to remain in those places with the sons of Manasseh. The reason for this failure is what is mentioned in (v. 21).

1.21.0.en: In the periods when the children of Israel grew strong, they put the Canaanites under tribute and made them work for them. But in all cases they did not drive them out from among them. The main reason is the weakness of the faith of the children of Israel in the power of God that supported them in driving out the pagans, in addition to their slackness and negligence in carrying out God's commandment. The result of this was that these peoples rose up against them afterward, humiliated them and seized their good things, as appears in the later events of this book.

1.22.0.en: Gezer: a city northwest of Jerusalem at a distance of 29 km (Map 12). The sons of Ephraim fell into the same error into which their brothers had fallen, for they left the Canaanites to dwell in their midst in the city of Gezer, which later became one of the most important cities of Ephraim.

1.23.0.en: Kitron: it lies about 11 km south of Haifa.

1.23.1.en: Nahalol: it lies south of Acre (Map 10). The tribe of Zebulun also failed to drive out the Canaanites, and the matter was limited to imposing tribute on them.

1.24.2.en: Ahlab: it lies northwest of Tyre.

1.24.3.en: Achzib: it lies north of Acre.

1.24.6.en: Rehob: to the east of Aphik (Map 10). The tribe of Asher also did not drive out the Canaanite inhabitants from the cities that fell within its portion of the land, and those cities are Zidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik and Rehob. And so the tribe of Asher dwelt with the Canaanites, the original inhabitants of the land.

1.25.0.en: Beth-shemesh: a city in the land of Naphtali, northeast of Nablus.

1.25.1.en: Beth-anath: a town in the land of Naphtali, east of Acre (Maps 10, 11). The same thing happened with the tribe of Naphtali, as if the contagion of slackness in driving out the pagan peoples had spread among them and they began to imitate one another. So Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh or the inhabitants of Beth-anath, but left them in their midst and was content to impose tribute on them.

1.25.2.en: The children of Israel left the pagan peoples to dwell in their midst, and this proved to be a calamity for them. So also we, if we leave a sin lurking inside our hearts, it will become a point of weakness, like a small hole through which the enemy of good slips in to gain strength against us afterward. May we be alert to these holes in our hearts and put an end to them, so that we do not give the devil a place.

1.26.0.en: The Amorites: a Semitic people who ruled parts of Palestine, and they were among the strongest of the Canaanite peoples.

1.26.1.en: When the tribe of Dan attacked the Amorite tribes, they gathered in the plains, so the tribe of Dan was confined to the mountainous places and was afraid to attack the Amorites gathered in the plains. So it grew slack and did not trust in God, and dwelt beside them.

1.27.0.en: Mount Heres: east of Jerusalem on the road to Jericho.

1.27.2.en: Shaalbim: east of the Jordan River, in the middle of its extent (Map 11). When the tribe of Dan was slack in driving out the Amorites, the Amorites dwelt in Mount Heres, in Aijalon and in Shaalbim. But it seems that the two tribes of the sons of Joseph were jealous for their brothers the Danites and grieved at their dwelling in the narrow mountain regions because of the siege imposed by the Amorites, so they helped their brothers the Danites and imposed their might upon the Amorites and forced them to pay tribute to the tribe of Dan. And because of the narrowness of the places the tribe of Dan had taken, it later fought Laish, which lies north of the land of the Jews, and they captured it as is clear in (Judg 18), and they called the city by the name of their father, Dan.

1.28.0.en: The ascent of Akrabbim: south of the Dead Sea.

1.28.1.en: Sela: to the south of the ascent of Akrabbim (Map 11). Before Joshua fought them, the Amorites occupied wide lands east of the Jordan, and the borders of their lands extended from the ascent of Akrabbim and Sela in the south to the far north.

1.28.2.en: When Satan sees slackness in the believer, he covets overcoming him. Therefore the believer must strive continually, resisting the forces of evil, armed with the whole armor of God according to the saying of Paul the Apostle, by practicing the sacraments of the Church, which give a person grace and strength in facing the forces of evil. The consequences of not driving out the inhabitants of the land are a summary of what happened repeatedly in the era of the Judges.
